headline_marked: DSCC unveils [[Tk 4,004 crore budget]] for 'Clean City, Green City'
headline: DSCC unveils Tk 4,004 crore budget for 'Clean City, Green City'
summary: The new budget prioritises dengue control, waterlogging mitigation, and environmental protection without imposing additional taxes on residents.
details: Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has announced a Tk 4,004.60 crore budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year. The plan focuses on the 'Clean City, Green City' initiative, prioritising civic services and environmental protection.

A significant increase in spending on mosquito control has been earmarked. This includes Tk 4 crore for fuel and lubricants for eradication efforts, and an increase in equipment and machinery allocation to Tk 7.5 crore.

DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam stated that the budget is realistic and implementable. He noted that no additional tax burden has been placed on city residents, instead introducing new revenue sources and rationalising expenditures.

Dengue prevention has been strengthened with daily larviciding and adult mosquito control across all wards. Monitoring teams have been formed for every ward and public awareness campaigns are ongoing through various channels.

To tackle waterlogging, DSCC has identified 33 hotspots across 75 wards. Short-term measures include cleaning drains and canals before monsoon, while portable pumps and suction machines are used during heavy rain.
For a long-term solution, the Institute of Water Modelling has been appointed to prepare a Drainage Master Plan for 57 DSCC wards.
caption:

headline: 11-party alliance to hold rally in Dhaka on August 5
summary: The Jamaat-e-Islami led coalition demands the implementation of the July National Charter and the results of the referendum.
details: An 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami has announced a rally in the capital's Paltan area on August 5. The decision was made during a liaison committee meeting held on Thursday at the residence of the opposition leader in Mintu Road.
caption:
A major political rally is coming to Dhaka. The 11-party alliance will gather at Paltan on August 5 to demand the implementation of the July National Charter.

An 11-party alliance led by Jamaat-e-Islami has announced a rally in the capital's Paltan area on August 5. The decision was made during a liaison committee meeting held on Thursday at the residence of the opposition leader in Mintu Road.
